newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia bonds find US a drag,no other incentives.
newsitem.headline: Australia bonds find US a drag,no other incentives.

text.p: *Australian bond yields rose following an easier tone in U.S. Treasuries, but with few other events to inspire interest, turnover is expected to be light.
*U.S. retails sales for June due later on Tuesday.
Australian bond yields rose following an easier tone in U.S. Treasuries on Monday, but with few other events to inspire interest, turnover is again expected to be light.

A dearth of major domestic data this week has left the market somewhat in limbo until next week's second quarter inflation and wages data, but hopes of a further easing in monetary policy is likely to prevent a full blown sell-off.
"The market is drifting a bit with some stock coming back on to the market. It looks like it's going to be a day of book squaring and book keeping," said one trader.

The U.S. market was slightly jittery ahead of June retail sales on Monday, which are expected to show a rebound after three consecutive monthly declines and amid reports of rising consumer confidence.
The market's failure to push down through 6.50 percent yield resistance on the U.S. 30-year bond also weighed on sentiment.
Meanwhile, the Australian Bureau of Statistics releases a series of partial indicators at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT) comprising manufacturing input prices, and export and import prices indices for May.

The local market's softer tone saw it underperform against the U.S., but it held its ground to Canada, which was also outpaced by the U.S. on Monday. Spreads widened to New Zealand bonds following today's release of the N.Z. quarterly CPI, which came in line with expectations at up 0.1 percent on the quarter.
